trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery. Report what is known; update as the review continues
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil, using a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate (252.204-7012(c)(3)); the report includes at least the elements listed on DIBNet
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Prime A subcontract includes the clause. The owner files. Not possible today without the certificate (POAM-009)

obligation: Review for compromise of covered defense information
trigger: Same trigger as the DoD report
deadline: Starts at discovery; results feed the report and its updates
notify: Internal (results go to DoD in the report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - identify compromised computers, data, and user accounts, including other systems that may have been accessed

obligation: Incident report number to Prime A
trigger: DIBNet report submitted and DoD assigns an incident report number
deadline: As soon as practicable
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - flowed down in the Prime A subcontract

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: As instructed by DC3 or the Contracting Officer. Do not send malware to the Contracting Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is found (a phishing kit may leave none on the owner's systems)

trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident
deadline: At least 90 days from submission of the report, so DoD can request the media or decline interest
notify: Internal custody (owner); on-call forensics firm; SaaS log exports
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - laptop image, SaaS audit exports, router logs

obligation: DoD access for forensic analysis and damage assessment
trigger: DoD request for more information or equipment; Contracting Officer request for damage assessment information
deadline: On request
notify: DoD (through the Contracting Officer, via Prime A)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the owner is the contact

trigger: Incident involving CUI in a cloud service
deadline: The provider must comply with paragraphs (c) to (g); coordinate so reports and preserved data match
notify: SYS-10 provider (support case and security contact from the CRM). SYS-01's commercial provider has no such duty, which is part of the gap
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - after migration; today the gap itself is reportable context

obligation: CMMC status and affirmation check after an incident
trigger: Incident shows the system no longer meets a requirement relied on in SPRS
deadline: Before the next SPRS entry or affirmation; a status is current only with no changes in compliance
notify: SPRS entry (owner as Affirming Official); Prime A if an affirmation is affected
applies_at_this_tier: Yes once a CMMC status exists; today update the SPRS score and date-to-110 if the incident changes them

citation: 22 CFR 127.12; export defined in 22 CFR 120.50; release defined in 22 CFR 120.56
trigger: Owner believes an ITAR violation may have occurred (for example, ITAR-marked drawings released to a foreign person)
deadline: Voluntary. Initial notice immediately after the violation is discovered; full disclosure within 60 calendar days of the notice unless an extension is granted (127.12(c)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the owner with export counsel. Theft by an outside attacker may not be the owner's violation; document the reasoning either way

trigger: Owner believes the EAR may have been violated (commercial aerospace data with EAR-controlled technology)
deadline: Voluntary; a deliberate decision not to disclose a significant apparent violation is an aggravating factor (764.5(a))
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the owner with export counsel

trigger: Commercial customer data affected
deadline: Per contract terms
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual, not legal. Check each agreement

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the business holds no personal information of others beyond business contact details. Recheck if the owner's own records or a customer's personal data are involved

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: No - fewer than 500 individuals' personal information is held

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - same reason as Florida. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live if personal information is involved

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy terms
applies_at_this_tier: No standalone cyber policy. Ask the professional liability carrier whether any cyber coverage applies before hiring outside help

trigger: Suspected theft of controlled technical information by a foreign or criminal actor
deadline: As soon as practical
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; coordinate with the DIBNet report

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. POL-01 10.6 requires counsel's advice first

obligation: Cleared defense contractor cyber incident on classified information system
trigger: Cyber incident on a classified information system
deadline: Immediately
applies_at_this_tier: No - no facility clearance or classified systems

obligation: Report discovery of covered telecommunications equipment/services during contract performance
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered by this incident type; applies only if such equipment is found (the clause is in the subcontract)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-04; not a current obligation
